messages:
monitor-bot: [ALERT] us-west-2 hosted-api: p95 latency spike detected for generation/v1 -> 1200ms (SLA 600ms). Start: 2026-03-17T02:12:01Z. Auto-paging oncall.

jessica: I'm paged, joining now. Collecting traces and trace-ids. @dan can you stand by for kernel/serving checks?

dan: looking at runtime dashboards — tail/worker latency increased immediately after the recent canary. QPS steady, GPUs not saturated. Kernel path fallback to slower CUDA kernels for seq > 1024. Pulling canary logs.

deploy-bot: deploy record: runtime canary 3.5.0-rc deployed to us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T01:58:40Z, 20% traffic. Triggered by pipeline #runtime-ci-8821.

jessica: ok. if canary is the likely cause we should route traffic off it. Proposal: route affected generation traffic to stable-3.4.2 or isolate canary to dedicated pool. @dan which is faster?

dan: routing is faster. executing: `rbtree set-route generation/v1 us-west-2->stable-3.4.2` against config-api. Applying now (cmd shown).

rita: product ops — we need a short status page blurb + customer notification draft. Keep it brief: "Investigating increased generation latency in us-west-2, mitigation in progress, no data loss." Add ETA once we have trend.

leo: support sees ~5 incoming tickets for latency; one customer flagged urgent (enterprise). Holding a brief note for them. Please include ETA.

jessica: route-change applied. Observability: p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 650ms within ~90s after route. Still slightly above 600ms SLO but trending down. Monitoring 10m window for stability.

dan: quick root cause: new kernel selection logic in 3.5.0-rc incorrectly selects fused attention fallback for long sequences, sending requests down slower execution path. Initiating rollback of canary to undo change. Command: `kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deploy/runtime-canary`

monitor-bot: metric update: us-west-2 generation/v1 p95 = 540ms (10:05 since incident start).

caroline: customer success draft to affected customers: "We're investigating elevated latency for generation API in us-west-2. We've applied traffic mitigation and are observing improvements. No data loss. We expect normal performance within 15 minutes; we'll follow up when fully resolved." Approving send.

jessica: planning handoff: I'll be oncall until 03:00 UTC then hand to @mike. Documenting actions taken and follow-ups: 1) rollback canary; 2) route fallback; 3) perf gating requirement for future canaries.

mike: taking over at 03:00 UTC. Please assign a postmortem owner for follow-up and timeline. Recommend owner: @dan + @rita for mitigation + communication. Also recommend adding a perf check in canary healthchecks (seq=1024 pass).

rita: proposed status page entry (short):
```
Summary: Elevated generation p95 latency in us-west-2 caused by a kernel selection regression introduced in a runtime canary.
Impact: Increased latency for a subset of hosted API requests (some customers may see degraded p95).
Mitigation: Routed traffic to stable kernel and rolled back canary.
Status: Mitigating -> Monitoring.
ETA: improvements expected within 15-30 minutes; investigating root cause and follow-up.
```

leo: customer notes sent to affected accounts (refs: #8342, #8343). No escalations pending.

jessica: closing immediate paging — p95 steady at ~520ms across us-west-2 for the past 5m. Leaving incident open for postmortem and action items. Last check-in before handoff.

mike: acknowledged. I will file the postmortem, include timeline, rollouts affected, and remediation actions (canary perf gate + telemetry alert for kernel fallback).

monitor-bot: incident timeline snapshot saved to incident-board (id: inc-3925004321).

jessica: thanks team. Leaving notes in incident doc and will sync with @dan/@rita for follow-up.
